To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The most common type of hypertext system is a document system, which is used by 60% of the users.

(1) the use of a hypertext system can be improved by the use of an adequate user interface and that (2) the user interface of hypertext systems can be improved by a careful consideration of the underlying data model.
the use of a hypertext system is influenced by: (i) the user interface, (ii) the user's task and the user's knowledge, (iii) the hypertext system's data model and (iv) the hypertext structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (a) the design of an object-based hypermedia system, (b) the development of a hypertext editor, (c) the development of hypertext applications and (d) the evaluation of hypertext systems.
the development of an architecture for a hypertext system which is capable of handling a wide range of different types of documents.
the design of hypertext systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the design of a user interface is a complex task which requires a lot of experience, a lot of creativity and a lot of knowledge about the application domain and the users.
the design of the user interface in a hypertext system is determined by the underlying logical structure, the data model.
the design of a hypertext system is not a trivial task and that the design of the interface is not the only important issue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have tried to find a good balance between the two main aspects, which are often considered to be in contradiction.
the user interface of a hypertext system has to be adapted to the logical structure of the underlying data model.
the user interface design of a hypertext system is determined by the data model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a method to generate a high-quality, large-scale dataset for evaluating the effectiveness of a variety of NLP models for the task of question answering.
we can achieve the same level of performance as a state-of-the-art hand-crafted model, while being more robust to hyperparameter tuning and more interpretable, thanks to its simple design.
we need to think about the design of a new generation of hypertext systems that support a broader range of user activities than just reading and writing.
